Landing.faqA1: In gasless mode, customers don't need POL or ETH — they pay with just their JPYC or USDC balance (that's what "gasless" means here). For JPYC gasless payments, a per-transaction OpenPay usage fee applies (1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum), deducted at settlement and split to OpenPay's designated wallet within the same transaction (the principal price of goods still transfers directly from the customer's wallet to the merchant's wallet; OpenPay does not hold sales). The store bears the fee, so the customer pays only the displayed amount and the merchant's net amount is the payment less the fee (the customer simply signs the transfer in JPYC). For tips to creators, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC; the 1% does not apply) is borne by the customer sending the tip. For USDC payments, the customer pays gas in USDC to the paymaster, so OpenPay does not collect a gas-equivalent (USDC gasless requires an EIP-7702-capable smart-account wallet; ordinary wallets fall back to standard payment where the customer pays their own gas — JPYC gasless works with any wallet). Cross-chain payments (paying from a different source chain) are not gasless — the source chain's network fee (ETH/POL etc.) is paid by the customer.
Landing.faqQ2: Can I receive both JPYC and USDC?
Landing.faqA2: Yes. JPYC is a good fit when you want JPY-denominated receipts; USDC is better for Web3-savvy or international customers. JPYC (JPY-pegged) is supported on Polygon / Kaia / Avalanche; USDC on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism / Polygon / Ethereum / Avalanche. Pick the chain in the QR builder. If the customer holds the token on a different chain, Circle CCTP V2 settles cross-chain automatically.
Landing.faqQ3: What if the customer has no wallet?
Landing.faqA3: Direct them to a browser wallet (MetaMask, Rabby, etc.) or a mobile wallet (MetaMask Mobile / Rainbow / Coinbase Wallet). OpenPay auto-detects multiple wallets via EIP-6963.
Landing.faqQ4: How do I convert JPYC / USDC to JPY?
Landing.faqA4: JPYC redeems 1:1 at <jpycEx>JPYC EX</jpycEx>. USDC can be sold via SBI VC Trade and other Japanese exchanges. The bottom of the <create>Receive</create> page lists exchange links per token.
Landing.faqA5: History is kept only in your browser's LocalStorage — never sent to OpenPay servers. You can export to CSV from the history page. Transaction hashes are recorded so you can verify on Etherscan / Polygonscan.
Landing.faqA6: The OpenPay usage fee. For JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas), a per-transaction OpenPay usage fee applies (1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum), deducted at settlement and split to OpenPay's designated wallet within the same transaction (the principal price of goods is sent directly to the merchant's wallet; OpenPay does not hold sales). The store bears this fee, and the customer pays only the displayed amount (for tips to creators, the gas-equivalent amount — about 2 JPYC; the 1% does not apply — is borne by the customer sending the tip). Paths where the customer pays gas themselves (e.g. USDC), and Standard (with-gas) payments, are not in scope (free). Note: if you use the mobile-order feature (in-store/kiosk and pre-order mobile ordering), the OpenPay usage fee is charged at a different rate — the mobile-order system fee (1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk; 3% for pre-order, gas included) — applied instead of, not in addition to, the gasless usage fee, regardless of the payment path (for pre-order, either store-borne or added to the customer total depending on the store setting). See the Terms of Service and the Specified Commercial Transactions Act disclosure for details.
Landing.faqA7: Both are stablecoins — digital currencies you can send and receive on a blockchain, whose value tracks a fiat currency. JPYC tracks the Japanese yen (1 JPYC ≈ 1 JPY), so you receive in yen terms. USDC, issued by Circle, tracks the US dollar (1 USDC ≈ 1 USD) and is widely used worldwide. Unlike Bitcoin and the like, their value is pegged to fiat, so you can use them for payments without worrying about price swings.
Landing.trustBody: OpenPay is built on a non-custodial design (funds are never held by OpenPay) and open-source stablecoin payment technology. All source code is MIT-licensed and public on GitHub — anyone can verify how the payment flow works.
Landing.trustTechStack: Tech stack: EIP-3009 signature relay (self-hosted relayer / Gelato fallback — JPYC gasless) / Circle Paymaster (USDC gasless — gas paid in USDC) / Circle CCTP V2 & Gateway (USDC cross-chain) / ERC-4337 (account abstraction) / ERC-7702 (EOA → smart account delegation) / Pimlico bundler/paymaster (fallback) / viem / wagmi / permissionless.js / Next.js

Landing.benefitsSubtitle: Real value for merchants, simplicity for customers.
Landing.benefitsFeeBody: OpenPay's per-transaction usage fee on JPYC gasless payments. It is 1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum, deducted at settlement. That's lower than typical credit-card (3.24%) or code-payment (1.98%) rates (representative examples).
Landing.benefitsCostBody: No POS terminal, no contracts, no upfront fees. Just one wallet address — go from start to a printed QR the same day.
Landing.benefitsSettlementBody: Sales land in the merchant wallet the moment the on-chain transaction confirms. No month-end closing, no 2–3 business day waits (non-custodial: OpenPay never holds funds).
Landing.benefitsNoSignupBody: Customers pay with just a wallet — no address, phone or email registration required. No KYC either.
Landing.benefitsWhyLead: Wallet transfers are handy for people who can already send crypto, but they fall short as store payments: you type the recipient and amount by hand, you can pick the wrong chain or token, the store can't easily confirm what a payment is for, and you need a separate token for gas. OpenPay is an open-source payment tool that removes the friction of using wallet transfers at the point of sale.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint1Body: The store bakes the payment conditions into a QR up front, and the customer just scans it. No hand-typing the recipient, amount, chain or token — so the slip-ups that plague raw wallet transfers go away.
Landing.benefitsWhyPoint2Body: Set a preset or any billed amount and present a clear "pay this amount" QR. Customers don't enter the amount themselves, which makes it practical at a counter or an event.

gasHint.body: Sending received JPYC / USDC to an exchange requires a small amount of native gas on each chain (POL on Polygon, ETH on Base / Arbitrum / Optimism). With MetaMask's Swap (Gas Station) feature, you can swap on Polygon / Base / Arbitrum without holding any POL or ETH — the gas fee is paid out of your JPYC or USDC. On chains where Gas Station is not available (e.g. Optimism), a small amount of ETH is required separately to initiate the swap.
gasHint.disclaimer: Note: Availability, supported chains, and success of MetaMask features depend on MetaMask itself; OpenPay is not involved. Network congestion or unsupported token routes on any chain may cause the swap to fail.

Terms.intro: These Terms of Service (the "Terms") govern your use of the blockchain payment service "{service}" (the "Service") operated by {company} (the "Company"). By using the Service, you agree to be bound by these Terms.

article1.title: Article 1 (Application)
article1.body: These Terms apply to all relationships between users and the Company concerning the use of the Service. If the Company separately establishes individual rules on the Service, such individual rules form part of these Terms; in case of conflict, individual rules prevail.

article2.title: Article 2 (Definitions)
article2.body: (1) "Merchant" means a business or individual who receives Supported Token payments through the Service. (2) "Customer" means a person who pays a Merchant through the Service. (3) "Wallet" means a self-custodial crypto wallet (EOA or smart contract account) controlled by the user. (4) "Supported Token" means a digital asset supported by the Service, currently including JPYC, an electronic payment instrument issued by JPYC Inc. as a funds transfer service provider registered under Japan's Payment Services Act, and USDC, a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (5) "Network Fee" means gas required to confirm a blockchain transaction. (6) "Gasless Payment" means a payment mode in which the Customer can complete payment without separately holding a native token (POL, ETH, etc.), and includes (a) paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee using an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar (e.g. JPYC payments), and (b) paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token via an ERC-4337 ERC20 Paymaster (e.g. USDC payments). (7) "Standard Payment (with Gas)" means a payment mode in which the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee and the Customer pays it from their own wallet.

article3.title: Article 3 (Nature of the Service)
article3.body: The Service is a non-custodial tool that facilitates transfers of Supported Tokens between user wallets. The Company never holds user funds. All transfers are executed on-chain via the user's own signature. The Company does not issue or operate the Supported Tokens, the underlying blockchains, or the wallet applications used by users. The Service consists of generating EIP-681 payment URIs, QR codes, batching user operations under the ERC-4337 standard, and relaying gas sponsorship; the Company does not intermediate in the underlying user-to-user transaction itself. The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds payable from Customer to Merchant. In a payment through the Service, the price of goods and similar amounts are transferred directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet. Separately, in Gasless Payment paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) via an ERC-4337 Paymaster or similar, or via an EIP-3009 technical relay (JPYC payments), the Company charges a per-transaction usage fee (the "OpenPay usage fee") to Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments, as consideration for use of the Service. The OpenPay usage fee is 1% (10 per 1,000) of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC. The OpenPay usage fee is taken at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement), split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip (only in this case does the Customer add the gas-equivalent amount on top of the tip). The OpenPay usage fee is consideration for use of the Service, not for the purpose of recovering gas, and is not linked to the actual gas amount. The Company receives only the OpenPay usage fee portion; the principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) is transferred directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet. In paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company. No OpenPay usage fee arises for the act of receiving a payment itself, for use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, or for paths where the Customer pays the Network Fee in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC). However, for JPYC payments checked out via the register (in-store POS) feature, from the July 2026 usage period the same OpenPay usage fee as gasless (1% of the payment) is charged as consideration for use of the Service (the register and other payment systems), even in Standard (with-gas) mode (deducted from the merchant's receipt; the customer still pays their own gas). Payment QR (/pay), tips to creators, the USDC route, and manually created payment links remain out of scope (free). For transactions made in Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it from their own wallet. The handling of gas in any of the above paths is a feature of the Service and does not constitute custody or management of user assets by the Company.

This fee is charged per mobile-order payment regardless of the payment path (whether gasless or standard, and therefore even for standard payments where the Customer pays the Network Fee themselves); the rate is 1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk and 3% for pre-order mobile ordering. For pre-order mobile ordering, depending on the store setting, either the store bears the fee out of the amount it receives (the Customer pays only the price of goods) or the Customer pays it on top of the price of goods. In either case the principal price of goods is transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales), and only the fee portion is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. section1.title: 1. Information We Collect
section1.body: We collect the following information in connection with the Service: (1) blockchain wallet addresses that the Company observes when users connect their wallet to the Service; (2) server log information including browser information, IP address, referrer, access timestamps, and page navigation; (3) anonymized statistics collected by Vercel Analytics, such as page views, visitor country/region, and device type; (4) email address and inquiry content when users contact us; (5) on-chain transaction information generated or referenced through the Service (such as transaction hash, sender wallet address, recipient wallet address, supported token, supported chain, transfer amount, OpenPay usage fee, payment mode, and payment status); (6) if the user grants camera permission on pages such as /scan for QR code reading, the camera video frames and the decoded QR string. To provide the Service's functionality, the Company may store in the user's browser local storage settings related to display and payments, transaction history, payment receipts, wallet connection state, and similar data. Such data is used within the client (the user's device) and is not transmitted to the Company's servers, nor used for cross-site behavioral tracking or advertising. The Company does not use tracking or advertising cookies. For features that involve sign-in (where used), the Company may use session cookies necessary to provide those features. The Company does not collect special-care-required personal information (such as race, creed, social status, medical history, or criminal record). The Company also does not carry out automated decision-making (including profiling) regarding users. Users may delete this client-side data at any time by clearing their browser cache or storage, or by using the deletion features within the Service (such as deleting payment receipts or transaction history).

section2.title: 2. Purposes of Use

Of the decoded results, only the OpenPay URL category that the Service recognizes (pay / tip / checkout / handle / order / external / eip681 / unknown) is sent to Sentry as an error-observation breadcrumb; the raw QR string and the user's wallet address are not sent to Sentry. The Company configures its error monitoring not to send personally identifying information, and if unnecessary personal data is nonetheless included in an error log, it will take reasonable measures such as deletion or masking.

section3.title: 3. Sharing with Third Parties and Service Providers
section3.body: We do not share personal information with third parties without user consent or where required by law. However, we engage the following service providers to operate the Service, all of which we supervise as required by the APPI: - Vercel Inc. (United States): hosting, CDN, analytics. - Pimlico Labs Inc. (United States): ERC-4337 bundler and paymaster service. - Circle Internet Financial, Inc. (United States): Circle Paymaster (ERC-4337 paymaster) service for USDC gasless payments. The customer pays the gas-equivalent amount in USDC to that paymaster; the Company does not collect or receive that fee. - Alchemy Insights Inc. (United States): blockchain RPC. Because these providers are located in the United States, personal information may be transferred to a third party located in a foreign country (APPI Article 28). Information on the personal data protection regime in the United States is published by the Personal Information Protection Commission of Japan in its "Survey on Foreign Personal Information Protection Regimes." We have data protection agreements in place with these providers and have implemented measures to protect users' rights and interests.

section4.title: 4. Retention Period
section4.body: We retain collected information only for the period necessary to fulfill the purposes of use. Server logs are deleted in sequence 90 days after collection. Inquiry records are deleted 3 years after the last correspondence. On-chain transaction records, by their nature, are permanently public outside our control, and we cannot delete them.

sectionPush.title: 5. Web Push Notifications (optional)
sectionPush.body: Users may optionally enable push notifications for received payments. Only if enabled, the Company stores in its KV storage the mapping between the user's wallet address and the push subscription endpoint (endpoint and encryption keys) issued by the browser. Up to 5 devices are stored per wallet, the mapping automatically expires after 90 days, and users can delete it at any time by disabling notifications. Notifications are delivered via the push service operated by the browser vendor (such as Apple, Google, or Mozilla). Whether the sale amount is included in the notification body is an optional user setting (off by default); only when turned on does the amount appear on the lock screen and similar surfaces. In logs, the subscription endpoint is recorded as a hash rather than retained in the clear.

sectionSecurity.title: 6. Security Measures for Personal Information
sectionSecurity.body: To prevent the leakage, loss, or damage of acquired personal information and otherwise ensure its safe management, the Company implements necessary and appropriate security measures, including encryption of communications via SSL/TLS, management of access privileges, measures against unauthorized access, and necessary and appropriate supervision of service providers.

section5.title: 7. Requests for Disclosure, Correction, and Suspension of Use
section5.body: Users may request disclosure, correction, addition, deletion, suspension of use, erasure, or suspension of third-party provision of their personal information held by us, pursuant to APPI Articles 33 through 35. For request procedures and fees, please contact us at the address shown in Section 8. We may require identity verification before responding.

section6.body: For inquiries regarding this Policy or requests under APPI: Operator: {company}. Address: {address}. Personal Information Manager: {representative}. Email: {email}.

section7.title: 9. Amendments to this Policy
section7.body: We may amend this Policy in response to changes in law, changes to the Service, or other necessary reasons. Amended Policies take effect when posted on the Service.

price.label: Consideration for the Service (OpenPay Usage Fee)
price.value: The OpenPay usage fee is a per-transaction usage fee borne by Merchants who use JPYC gasless payments (where the Company sponsors the gas). It is 1% of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC (the fee is triggered by JPYC gasless usage, and paths where the Customer pays gas themselves—e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster—are not in scope). The OpenPay usage fee is taken, as consideration for using the Service (payment processing, merchant QR code generation, the checkout UI, supported wallet integration, gas sponsorship and payment relay, and operation and maintenance), at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement), split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip. The Company receives only the OpenPay usage fee portion; the principal price of goods and similar amounts continues to be transferred directly to the Merchant's wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales). Costs per payment mode are as follows. (1) Gasless Payment mode: in paths where the Company sponsors the Network Fee (gas) (e.g. JPYC payments), the Company sponsors that Network Fee and charges the OpenPay usage fee above (the OpenPay usage fee is not for the purpose of recovering gas and is not linked to the actual gas amount). The principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) is transferred directly to the Merchant's wallet. In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and the Company does not collect it. (2) Standard Payment (with Gas) mode: the Company does not sponsor the Network Fee; the Customer pays it in the native token from their own wallet. No OpenPay usage fee arises for the act of receiving a payment itself, for the use of Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, or for paths where the Customer pays gas themselves (e.g. USDC via the ERC20 Paymaster). However, for JPYC payments checked out via the register (in-store POS) feature, from the July 2026 usage period the same OpenPay usage fee as gasless (1% of the payment) is charged as consideration for use of the Service (the register and other payment systems), even in Standard (with-gas) mode (deducted from the merchant's receipt; the customer still pays their own gas). Payment QR (/pay), tips to creators, the USDC route, and manually created payment links remain out of scope (free). In addition, if you use the mobile-order feature (in-store / kiosk ordering and pre-order mobile ordering), the Company applies a different rate of the OpenPay usage fee for use of the mobile-order feature (including the shop page, menu, order management, and order relay): it does not charge this in addition to the gasless usage fee above, but applies only the following rate (this rate is the mobile-order system fee; where the Company sponsors gas for a gasless mobile order, that gas is included in this rate, and the gasless usage fee above is not charged again on top). This fee is charged per mobile-order payment regardless of the payment path (whether gasless or standard, and therefore even for standard payments where the Customer pays the Network Fee themselves); the rate is 1% of the payment for in-store/kiosk and 3% for pre-order mobile ordering. For pre-order mobile ordering, depending on the store setting, either the store bears the fee out of the amount it receives (the Customer pays only the price of goods) or the Customer pays it on top of the price of goods. In either case the principal price of goods is transferred directly to the Merchant's designated wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales), and only the fee portion is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. This mobile-order system fee was introduced on June 17, 2026 and applies to use of the mobile-order feature on and after the day the feature becomes available; /pay payment links, tips to creators, and standard payment links other than mobile order are not in scope. In addition, for use of the x402 facilitator operated by the Company for AI agents and developers (a function that intermediates HTTP 402-based per-request billing for APIs and content, including resource registration, a public catalog (discovery), payment verification, on-chain settlement, and receipt issuance), the Company charges an "x402 facilitator fee" as consideration for use of the Service (the facilitator). The x402 facilitator fee is 1% of the payment with a minimum of 2 JPYC, and applies to use on and after the day the x402 facilitator feature becomes available. The fee is added on the buyer's side (the payer) on top of the listed price (the seller—i.e., the resource registrant—receives the listed price in full). It is split to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction at the time each payment is executed (on-chain settlement), and the principal price is transferred directly to the seller's designated wallet (the Company does not receive, hold, or settle sales). Network fees (gas) the Company sponsors for gasless settlement are included in this fee. This x402 facilitator fee was newly established on June 28, 2026; it is a separate consideration, independent of the OpenPay usage fee and the mobile-order system fee, and only this fee applies to x402 payments. /pay payment links, tips to creators, in-store payments, and mobile ordering are not subject to this x402 facilitator fee.

additionalFees.label: Additional Costs
additionalFees.value: (1) Network fees (gas): fees required for confirming transactions on the blockchain. In Gasless Payment mode, the user may be able to pay without separately holding native tokens such as POL or ETH. Specifically, in paths where the Company sponsors gas (e.g. JPYC payments) the Company sponsors that gas and does not separately collect a gas-equivalent amount from the user, but a per-transaction OpenPay usage fee applies to such payments as consideration for the Service (see "Consideration for the Service" above). In paths where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token (e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC), the Customer pays the gas to the Paymaster provider in USDC or similar, and the Company does not collect it. In Standard Payment (with Gas) mode, the Customer pays the Network Fee in the native token (POL, ETH, etc.) from their own wallet. (2) Wallet application fees: governed by the terms of the wallet application chosen by the user. (3) Communication costs: internet connection charges and communication costs required to use the Service are borne by the user.

serviceStartTiming.label: Service Provision Timing
serviceStartTiming.value: Service to a Merchant begins when the Merchant connects a wallet and generates a QR code. Payment between Customer and Merchant is completed when the Customer scans the QR, approves the transfer in their wallet, and the transaction is finalized on-chain.

paymentTiming.label: Payment Timing and Method
paymentTiming.value: Payments through the Service are transferred on-chain directly from the Customer's wallet to the Merchant's designated wallet at the time each transaction is executed. In JPYC Gasless Payment where the Company sponsors gas, the OpenPay usage fee (consideration for use of the Service; 1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum) is taken at the time each payment is executed (at on-chain settlement) by an on-chain split of a Supported Token (JPYC) from the Merchant's wallet to a wallet designated by the Company within the same transaction. The OpenPay usage fee is borne by the Merchant (the Customer pays only the displayed payment amount, and the fee is deducted from the amount the Merchant receives); the net amount the Merchant receives is the payment amount less the OpenPay usage fee. For tips to creators, however, the gas-equivalent amount (about 2 JPYC per transaction; the 1% of the payment does not apply) is borne by the Customer sending the tip. For the principal price of goods and similar amounts (excluding the OpenPay usage fee), no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company (and where the Customer pays gas in a Supported Token, e.g. the ERC20 Paymaster for USDC, that fee is paid to the Paymaster provider and no transfer is made to a wallet designated by the Company). If for any reason the Company cannot collect the OpenPay usage fee, the Company may suspend gasless payment relay for that Merchant (the act of receiving a payment itself and Standard Payment (with Gas) mode remain available). The Company does not receive, hold, manage, or later settle the price of goods, service fees, or other sales proceeds (excluding the OpenPay usage fee) payable to Merchants. The Company does not issue separate invoices, hold funds in escrow, operate a prepaid charge system, or settle merchant sales. The only payment method for the Service is on-chain transfer of Supported Tokens (such as JPYC / USDC); credit cards, bank transfers, cash, and other payment methods are not supported.

returnPolicy.label: Refunds and Cancellations
returnPolicy.value: Due to the technical nature of blockchain, finalized transfers (including transfers of the price of goods) cannot, in principle, be cancelled, refunded, or modified. The OpenPay usage fee is consideration for use of the Service, including payment processing, gas sponsorship and payment relay in Gasless Payment mode, and mitigation of network-fee volatility risk, and is taken at the time each payment is executed within the same transaction, so it is, in principle, non-refundable after the payment is finalized (a fee of 1% of the payment with a 2 JPYC minimum applies per payment). The OpenPay usage fee is not for the purpose of recovering gas and is not linked to the actual gas amount, so no difference settlement against gas arises. Before submitting, users must verify the destination address, amount, supported token, supported chain, payment mode, and the OpenPay usage fee shown. The "CSV 24-hour pass" (100 JPYC per purchase, valid for 24 hours from the time of payment), purchasable after the accounting CSV download feature is enabled, is a prepaid optional right to use and is non-refundable (no refunds or prorated refunds after payment). The CSV pass does not auto-renew, and re-purchasing grants 24 hours from the new payment time and does not stack onto any remaining time; paying more than 100 JPYC still grants only 24 hours of validity. If the Service is unusable due to a material defect, please contact us by email; we will investigate and respond within a reasonable scope. The Service is a beta version provided "as is," and the Company does not provide any special warranty (including warranty against defects) for the Service (see the Disclaimer and Terms of Service for details). Furthermore, any dispute concerning defects, non-delivery, quantity discrepancies, or cancellation of goods or services paid for through the Service shall be resolved directly between the merchant and the customer; the Company is not a party to such sales contracts and bears no liability for them.
